L.S.
c. J.S.

2011 QCCS 6123

SUPerior

JR1353

COURt

CANADA

PROVINCE
of QUÉBEC

DISTRICT
of

MONTREAL

N°:

500-14-037905-114

DATE :

November 8, 2011

_________________________________________________________________________

presiding:
the HONORABLE BRIAN RIORDAN, J.S.C.

_________________________________________________________________________

L... S...

Applicant

v.

J...
S...

Respondent

and

S... S...

Reasonable Member of the Family

and

THE
PUBLIC CURATOR OF QUÉBEC

Mis en cause

judgment ON MOTION FOR

PROTECTIVE SUPERVISION OF A MAJOR PERSON

and safeguard order

[
1
]

Applicant ("
L...
") alleges that
his sister ("
J...
"
[1]
) is partially
incapacitated and totally unable to administer her property.  He thus requests
the Court to order the convocation of a family council comprised of six family
members and friends and to appoint him as tutor having the power to administer J...'s
property and assets.

[
2
]

J... contests vigorously.  She does not want L...
to be involved in her life.  Her position is complicated in this respect,
however, since she is living in the house that their mother left to them
"in equal proportions"
in her will prior to her death on March 6, 2010 (the "
Will
").
The house is situated at […] in city A, Québec (the
"
Property
").

[
3
]

Adopting the recent tactics of protestors around
the world, J... has "occupied Street A" since the mother's death.
She refuses not only to allow access to L... or any other person, but also to
discuss any matters dealing with it, the mother's estate or just about anything
else.

[
4
]

Because of her obstinacy, on August 3
rd

of this year L... obtained a Safeguard Order (the "
First Order
")
from the Superior Court authorizing him generally to do all that is reasonably
required to permit him, as executor of the Will, to administer and settle the
estate with respect to the Property and its contents.  Undaunted, J... refuses
to respect the First Order and bars all access to the Property.

[
5
]

To add further complications to L...'s life, she
refuses to sign any documents needed to settle the mother's estate and won't
accept disbursement of any of the substantial amount that is due to her under
it.  She says she contests the Will, particularly the clause by which the
mother stipulates that her (J...'s) share will be held in trust by L... and
"distributed to her for her welfare in
such manner as he considers advisable"
.  She also
objects to the stipulation that any part of her share still held in trust at
the time of her death will go to L... or, if predeceased, to his children.

[
6
]

To accept any amounts from the estate, she
fears, would constitute acquiescence in the Will and weaken her contestation,
which for the moment remains strictly oral.

[
7
]

Two expert witnesses testified in support of the
present motion, a psychiatrist and a social worker from the Jewish General
Hospital.  While fully recognizing their good faith and honest desire to assist
J..., the Court did not find their testimony sufficiently convincing to
justifying granting the motion.

[
8
]

Both opined that J... is totally unable to
administer her property and partially unable to protect her person and exercise
her civil rights.  Given these written opinions, it is somewhat surprising that
neither expert questioned L...'s amendment to the present motion by which he
desisted in the request for a curatorship to the person and limited his request
to a tutorship with respect to J...'s property.

[
9
]

Their testimony focused in great part on her
lack of cooperation with respect to the Property, yet neither one had much
first-hand knowledge of J... or of her living situation.  The psychiatrist had
never been to the Property and had seen J... only a few times in the hospital,
the last time being in May, 2010.  He based his March 14, 2011 opinion on
information he had received from the social worker and L....

[
10
]

The social worker had spoken to her more
recently, but not often.  She admitted having visited the Property only once,
in early 2010 before the mother's death, and that at that time, in spite of a
few bags of garbage in the kitchen, she
"had seen worse"
.
She pointed out that J... was not cooperative in response to her requests that
she (J...) come to the hospital for consultations, but that is hardly cause for
imposing tutorship with respect to her assets.

[
11
]

More to the point, the social worker replied in
the negative to the Court's question as to whether she had seen any indication
that J... had acted irresponsibly in her financial dealings - other than with
respect to the Property.  She later added, however, that she thought her
refusals to advise L... of the number of her bank account and to cash cheques
from the estate and from social welfare showed financially irresponsible
behaviour.  Even if that did, does this justify stripping her of her right to
manage her own property and assets?

[
12
]

Imposing tutorship on an adult person represents
a major intrusion into that person's life.  Such a step should not be taken
lightly or without convincing proof that it is necessary.  The proof here is
far from convincing.

[
13
]

From L...'s testimony and the oral pleadings of
his attorney, it is obvious that L...'s principal motive for the present motion
is to counter J...'s unreasonable refusals to cooperate in his efforts to
settle the estate.  She is holding the Property hostage by obstinately
preventing him from repairing and selling it, or even from seeing to its normal
upkeep.  She won't divulge the number of her bank account so that he can
deposit funds into it and she refuses even to talk to him.

[
14
]

J...'s behaviour is unacceptable and the Court
has great sympathy for L...'s situation.  She is pigheaded and unreasonable,
but she is also intelligent and coherent.  The remedy sought here is
inappropriate and disproportionate and, from a practical point of view, it
would not solve the problem.  L... would still have to seek court assistance to
evict J... and to find a means to transfer her half of the estate to her.  The
Court will thus dismiss the present motion.

[
15
]

But that does not mean that we will do nothing.
J... scoffs at the First Order and treats it, and the court that issued it,
with disdain.  We must intervene to ensure the respect of the law and the
court.

[
16
]

Under article 46 of the Code of Civil Procedure
[2]

and the inherent powers of the Superior Court, we have broad powers, even under
our own initiative, to issue orders to safeguard the rights of the parties.
One of L...'s clear rights in this file is to have the First Order respected by
J..., something that appears to be most unlikely in the absence of the Court's
intervention.

[
17
]

On September 15th, L... obtained authorization
to proceed against her by way of contempt of court, but we postponed that
proceeding both because of a lack of time and of a firm conviction that, even
were it granted, it would not resolve the outstanding issues.  A more practical
and rapid solution must be found.

[
18
]

The first step towards resolution is to have J...
obey the First Order, which will facilitate the following step of her moving
out of the Property so that it can be repaired and sold, unless she agrees to
purchase L...'s share of it.  One practical and expeditious way to enforce the
First Order is to issue a second Safeguard Order granting increased power to
ensure that the First Order will be obeyed.  This is what we propose to do.

[
19
]

Concerning the criteria applicable to Safeguard
Orders, they are all met here with little difficulty.

[
20
]

The urgency of the matter flows both from the
fact that winter is fast approaching, which requires that the Property be
inspected and repaired, as well as from J...'s consistent and stubborn refusal
to respect the First Order.  The Court is convinced that she will never comply
with it voluntarily.  It is thus time to act.

[
21
]

Irreparable harm is being caused to L... on a
number of fronts.  J...'s behaviour constitutes harassment of him.  He is
forced to spend much more time settling his mother's estate than would
otherwise be the case.  The value of his interest in the Property is threatened
in an incalculable way by J...'s delinquency with respect to maintenance and
repair.  All these represent irreparable harm.

[
22
]

Finally, the balance of inconvenience easily
favours the issuance of the order.  In the end, this order will facilitate and
quicken the settlement of the mother's estate, from which J... will receive one
half of a significant sum of money.  In that light, there will be absolutely no
inconvenience caused to her, whereas, if the order does not issue, L... will
continue to suffer the prejudice we outlined above.

[
23
]

Based on this analysis and given J...'s
behaviour to date and the attitude she demonstrated at trial, the Court is
justified in issuing a second Safeguard Order reinforcing her obligation to
comply with the First Order and authorizing the police to use whatever force is
reasonably required to that end, with access ensured by a locksmith or other
workmen.  Given her fault in this matter, any related expenses to implement the
orders will be charged to J...'s share of the mother's estate.

[
24
]

We shall also deal with two issues not covered
by the First Order: her failure to pay occupation rent to L... based on his
one-half interest in the Property and her failure to do proper maintenance and
upkeep on the Property.

[
25
]

Concerning an occupation rent, when L... causes
an evaluation of the market price of the Property to be done under the First
Order, he should also obtain an estimation of its
monthly fair-market rental value.  We shall authorize him to pay himself a rent
for J...'s occupation of the Property equal to one half of that estimated
rental value.  That rent will be paid out of J...'s share of the mother's estate,
starting as of April 1, 2010, the first full month after the mother's death.

[
26
]

As well, since the proof shows that J... is
delinquent with respect to all normal on-going maintenance of the Property,
such as grass cutting, snow removal etc., we shall authorize L... to have that
done at her sole expense.  Since she resides in the Property, she alone should
be responsible for those types of expenses, given that they are non-capital
items.

[
27
]

Before undertaking any of the actions permitted
under this order, L... will have to provide J... prior
written notice of twenty-four (24) hours, delivered
either personally or, where she does not answer the door for any reason, by
leaving it in her mailbox.

[
28
]

Finally, given that the present Safeguard Order
forms part of the liquidation of a succession, assists in the making of an
inventory and permits the execution of urgent repairs, all as foreseen in the
First Order, the Court will order its provisional execution notwithstanding
appeal.

[
29
]

BASED ON
THESE REASONS, the court:

[
30
]

DISMISSES

Applicant's Motion for Protective
Supervision of a Major Person;

[
31
]

issues
a Safeguard Order in light of Respondent's failure to respect the
Safeguard Order of August 3, 2010 in this file (the "
First Order
");

[
32
]

AUTHORIZES
Applicant, as well as any third party that he reasonably requires to
assist him, after prior notice to Respondent, to have full and unfettered
access to and in the immoveable property situated at […] in city A, Québec and
occupied by Respondent (the "
Property
") in order to execute
the following actions, and this, with or without Respondent's permission or
approval:

a.   any action authorized under the First Order;

b.   preparation of an estimation of the monthly fair
market rental value of the Property (the "
Estimated Monthly Rent
");

c.   all normal on-going maintenance, such as, without
limitation, grass cutting, snow removal etc.;

[
33
]

declares
that the cost of executing the actions authorized in the preceding
paragraph hereof will be advanced initially by Applicant and charged against
the estate of the parties' mother and reimbursed to Applicant from time to time
and as soon as it is legally possible to disburse funds from said estate,
except for the cost of normal maintenance, which shall be charged solely
against Respondent's share of the mother's estate;

[
34
]

AUTHORIZES
Applicant, in the event of Respondent's refusal to cooperate, to
engage the services of a locksmith or any other workman reasonably required in
order to gain access to any part of the Property in order to execute any action
authorized by the present Safeguard Order, with any cost related thereto to be
advanced initially by Applicant and charged solely against Respondent's share
of the mother's estate and reimbursed to Applicant from time to time and as
soon as it is legally possible to disburse funds from said estate;

[
35
]

ORDERS
all police
officers having jurisdiction in the circumstances, in the event of Respondent's
refusal to cooperate, to attend with Applicant or his mandatary at the Property
and to prevent Respondent, by physical force if necessary, from disrupting the
execution of any action authorized by the present Safeguard Order, and this,
upon simple oral request to that effect by Applicant, with
any cost related thereto to be advanced initially by Applicant and charged
solely against Respondent's share of the mother's estate and reimbursed to
Applicant from time to time and as soon as it is legally possible to disburse
funds from said estate;

[
36
]

DECLARES
that any prior notice required hereunder will be sufficient if
delivered to Respondent either personally or, where she does not answer the
door for any reason, by leaving it in her mailbox, in all cases at least
twenty-four (24) hours before the proposed action is to occur;

[
37
]

AUTHORIZES
Applicant to pay himself a monthly rental for Respondent's
occupation of the Property as of April 1, 2010 equal to one half (1/2) of the
Estimated Monthly Rent, such rental to be charged solely against Respondent's
share of the mother's estate and paid to Applicant from time to time and as
soon as it is legally possible to disburse funds from said estate;

[
38
]

ORDERS
the
provisional execution of the present Safeguard Order notwithstanding appeal.

[
39
]

the whole
with costs.

_____________________________

BRIAN RIORDAN, J.S.C.

Mtre. Glenn Derstenfeld

Attorney for Applicant

J... S...

Acting Alone

Hearing Date:  November
4, 2011

[1]
The Court adopts the attorneys' practice of referring to the
parties by their first names, since they have the same family name.  No
disrespect is intended.

[2]

46.
The courts and judges have all the powers necessary for the exercise
of their jurisdiction.

They
may, at any time and in all matters, whether in first instance or in appeal,
issue orders to safeguard the rights of the parties, for such time and on such
conditions as they may determine.  As well, they may, in the matters brought
before them, even on their own initiative, issue injunctions or reprimands,
suppress writings or declare them libellous, and make such orders as are
appropriate to deal with cases for which no specific remedy is provided by law.
